scenes.say: How do you get past a rival without ever passing him on track?
You're running second, a second behind the leader, and on a tight track there's no way past.
So your team brings you in one lap before him.
On their first lap, fresh tyres are a second or two quicker than worn ones.
While the leader does one more lap on old tyres, you make up the time. He comes out of the pits, and you're already ahead.
When new tyres are hard to warm up, the opposite works. You stay out longer and gain time in clean air.
Follow every driver's pit stops, tyre age and gaps live on LapRadar.

title: Undercut and overcut: getting past a rival without passing him on track
